title: Allama Iqbal, poet of the nation
takeaway: A poet's words can give a whole people the courage to stand tall.
scene: A short tribute to Allama Muhammad Iqbal, the poet-philosopher whose ideas helped bring Pakistan into being. Dr. Ahmad's own poetry borrows many of Iqbal's images, such as the royal falcon.

original: علموں تے کرداروں اچا سوہنے سخن اچیرے
قوم نوں جس عطا کر دتا رعب جلال نرالا
transliteration: Ilmon te kirdaaron uchcha, sohne sukhan uchere
Qaum nu jis ataa kar ditta raub jalaal niraala
translation: Great in learning and character, with beautiful, lofty words,
he gave the nation a rare dignity and majesty.
couplets.story: Iqbal was a giant in knowledge and in character, and his words were beautiful and inspiring. He gave his people a new sense of dignity and strength.

original: مسلم قوم نوں سب توں وکھرا درس خودی دا دتا
زندہ رہن دا سانوں دسیا عزم خیال نرالا
transliteration: Muslim qaum nu sab ton vakhra dars khudi da ditta
Zinda rehan da saanu dassiya azm khayaal niraala
translation: He gave the Muslim nation a lesson unlike any other: the lesson of selfhood (khudi).
He showed us a remarkable resolve and vision for how to truly live.
couplets.story: His big idea was 'khudi', having a strong, God-centred sense of who you are. He taught people how to live boldly, not just survive.

original: ہر پاسے اج تیکر جس دی پھیل رہی رشنائی
اچی تھاویں رکھ گیا اے دیوا بال نرالا
transliteration: Har paase ajj teekar jis di phail rahi rushnaai
Uchchi thaaveen rakh gaya ae deeva baal niraala
translation: His light is still spreading everywhere today:
he lit a remarkable lamp and set it up high.
couplets.story: His ideas are still lighting up the world today. It's as if he lit a special lamp and placed it high up where everyone can see it.

original: توصیفاں تعریفاں کردا ہر اک چھوٹا وڈا
احمدؔ راج اقبال دا مالک سی اقبال نرالا
transliteration: Tauseefaan taareefaan karda har ik chhota vadda
Ahmad raaj iqbaal da maalik si Iqbal niraala
translation: Everyone, young and old, sings his praises.
Ahmad, the remarkable Iqbal was master of the realm of good fortune.
couplets.story: Everyone, young and old, praises him. The poet ends with a play on words: 'iqbal' also means 'good fortune', and Iqbal truly ruled over it.

deeper: Iqbal's 'khudi' is a spiritual idea, not just a political one: a self made strong by its relationship with God. Dr. Ahmad's own poetry is full of Iqbal's influence, especially the royal falcon (shahbaz) soaring toward the Throne of God.
why: It introduces readers to Iqbal, the most important poet in Pakistan's history, and to his key idea, khudi.
prompt: What does having a strong sense of who you are mean to you?
notes: The last line puns on 'iqbal', which also means 'good fortune' or 'prosperity'.
